name: Middle Irish (900-1200)

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Middle Irish (10-12th century) (midd1360).

notes: Research. Goidelic (Insular Celtic) medieval stage written in the Latin alphabet. Grapheme map covers the basic vowels (with the acute marking length), the plain consonant letters, and the lenition digraphs ch/th/ph. The pervasive broad/slender (velarised vs palatalised) consonant contrast is not orthographically recoverable and is left unencoded; consonant lenition was written inconsistently in the manuscripts and only the h-digraphs are captured. Reconstructed phonetic values carry appreciable uncertainty, so a substantial PER floor is expected. Grapheme table checked against Thurneysen (1946): no discrepancy found.

stress.notes: Middle Irish, like Old Irish, has fixed word-initial stress (Thurneysen 1946, A Grammar of Old Irish): the first syllable of the word is stressed, with pretonic preverbal particles being proclitic (unstressed) rather than shifting the accent. `default_position=1` models the default case; proclitic preverb sequences are not separately handled for lack of a closed enumerable list applicable at the grapheme level.
